text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought two 54,000 tonne shipments of South American soybeans at a tender on Tuesday. Traders said bids were mostly for soybean supplies of South American origin, while a few that specified U.S. grain ranged between US$10-US$22 a tonne higher.
WHEAT SALE - Three Philippine mills bought a total of 25,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat through Japanese trading firm Marubeni Corp, Manila grains traders said.

BARLEY SALE - Malta bought 6,000 tonnes of feed barley on Tuesday at a tender for July 25-August 2 delivery, grain traders said. Unconfirmed trade indications put the price at just under $155 per tonne, cost and freight.

WHEAT TENDER - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd jointly invited tenders to buy a total of 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Wednesday, traders said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka seeks 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of PL-480 wheat for June 30-July 19 shipment. Offers are due by 1630 GMT June 5 at the Sri Lankan embassy in Washington.
DURUM TENDER - Algeria was scheduled to tender June 3 to buy 150,000 tonnes of optional durum wheat for shipment in July and August, European grain traders said.

CORN TENDER - Naseem Agriculture of Abu Dhabi seeks 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine or South African yellow maize for second half August shipment, South Africa's shippers association said. Bids are due June 6.

SOYMEAL AND TAPIOCA TENDERS - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation said it passed on a tender to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal due to high offer prices. The federation also passed on tenders for 30,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet, 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal and 52,000 tonnes of feed wheat because of higher than expected prices.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs seeks offers June 4 to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for July with confirmation on June 12.

MARKET TALK - Iraq on Monday night cancelled a purchase of 150,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat and apparently switched the purchase to 100,000 up to 150,000 tonnes of Australian hard wheat, several U.S. exporters said ... Philippine feed millers and livestock farmers plan to import more U.S. corn because of a supply shortage that is lifting domestic prices, industry officials and traders said ...

...The Australian Wheat Board expects Japan will continue to buy Australian wheat to fulfill an agreement for the purchase of about 900,000 tonnes this year. This was despite calls by the Food Agency of Japan, one of the AWB's largest customers, for a reduction in Australian wheat export prices....One of the Philippines' largest flour millers said on Tuesday it was seeking high protein break and noodle wheats because recent imports fell below its quality specifications.
